title: Clarify Firearm Storage Law
lastAction: Ref To Com On Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill clarifies North Carolina's firearm storage law to explicitly require safe storage of both loaded and unloaded firearms when minors have access to them. The change responds to a 2024 court ruling that found the law ambiguous about whether unloaded firearms stored near ammunition must be secured.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this clarification closes a dangerous loophole that put children at risk. They point to the tragic case cited in the bill where a teenager accessed an unloaded firearm stored next to ammunition and accidentally killed himself. Proponents contend the law's intent was always to prevent minors from accessing firearms in any readily-usable condition, and this clarification makes that intent clear while still requiring actual harm before criminal liability applies.
aiConArguments: Opponents may argue the clarification expands criminal liability for gun owners in their own homes and could criminalize storage practices that previously seemed legal. Some may contend that requiring secure storage of unloaded firearms—even when stored with ammunition—places additional burdens on lawful gun owners and may infringe on Second Amendment rights, or that the law should focus on parental responsibility rather than criminalizing storage methods.
